headline: Colossal Biosciences, a company that aims to bring extinct animals back, says its new AI tool has picked about 2,300 gene-edit targets to test for recreating the dodo.
score_reason: Interesting biotech application of AI, but company claims and untested predictions.
importance_line: It shows AI helping narrow gene-editing choices, mainly of interest to scientists and investors, while the targets are only predictions with no animal produced.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Colossal Biosciences, which works to bring extinct species back, has announced an AI platform called GenoMorph that predicts which genes to edit to give a living bird dodo-like features, and says it has found about 2,300 targets to test in the lab. CEO Ben Lamm told TechCrunch the tool does not edit genes itself and that no edit is assumed safe, so the predictions are unproven.
notes: Company claims relayed by TechCrunch; the 2,300 targets are predictions awaiting lab tests.
